match.reason: The new point asks students to study one chosen Australian right, its development and the laws that protect it, and none of the bank points teaches that case-study task; they cover general concepts such as types of rights, what human rights are, the history of rights, housing as a right and the bill of rights debate.

draft.title: Studying a human rights issue
card: A human rights issue is studied by picking one right and looking at how it applies in Australia. The right to vote is one example. Freedom of expression is another.
Studying how the right developed means tracing how it changed over time. For voting, this includes who was first allowed to vote and who was added later.
Studying how the right is protected means finding the laws that protect it. These can be Acts of Parliament, the Australian Constitution and court decisions.
Studying an issue also asks how well the right is protected today, and whether some people still miss out on it.
draft.remember: Study one right by asking how it developed, which laws protect it, and how well it is protected.

a.q: A student studies the right to vote in Australia. Which task is part of studying how the right developed?
opts: Tracing how the group of people allowed to vote changed
Listing the penalties for breaking a particular voting law
Comparing voting rules in two different school elections
Predicting which party will win the next federal election
a.why: Development is about change over time, such as who gained the vote and when. Listing penalties looks at how a law is enforced, not at how the right changed over time.

b.q: Ravi is studying freedom of expression in Australia. He reads an Act of Parliament and a High Court decision that protect it. What is Ravi studying?
opts: Which laws protect the right
How the right developed over time
How people disagree about the right
Which people campaigned for the right
b.why: Acts of Parliament and court decisions are laws that protect a right, so Ravi is studying its protection. Development would mean looking at how the right changed over time, which is a different task.
b.clue: An Act and a court decision are both kinds of law.

a.best: Tracing how the group of people allowed to vote changed
